CURRENT STATE, READ THIS FIRST (review-ajcr r4, 2026-07-30). Everything below
this block is the audit HISTORY: five layers of correction and self-correction,
in which the actual costing does not appear until roughly halfway down. It is
kept because each retraction is evidence, but a lane picking a target should
read this block and then jump to the header "THE COSTING, RE-RANKED".
================================================================================

THE MACHINE IS SOUND AND HAS NOTHING TO FEED IT. pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy
(Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are sorry-free, kernel-confirmed, non-circular,
and WOULD produce a representing scheme. All three antecedents are undischarged
and no sorry-free witness exists for any of them.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS, ranked by measured cost, cheapest last:
 1. IsChartUniv (the per-index chart certificate, `hf`) -- CERT-Sigma-gated.
    Refuted at V = top and free-but-useless at V = bot; whether the PAIR holds at
    any V strictly between is UNMEASURED at every V. Inhabitation at one concrete
    V is the open question. Rows: chart-u, chart-restrict, atlas-coupling.
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc f (DAT-B coverage) -- the most
    expensive, and multi-round (told to the human as I-1090). Cannot be discounted
    by restricting the atlas: ajcr-p1's isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono carries
    any V up to top, where the inclusion is an iso. Restricted coverage is no
    cheaper than unrestricted -- and note only ONE direction is proved, so it is
    as measured STRICTLY STRONGER. Row: dat-b.
 3. rep i (a representation of divFunctor at each parameter) -- the divisor-
    representability lane's target. Rows: ddr.divrep (+ u2, abel-widened).

RIDERS THAT ARE NOT SEPARATE OBLIGATIONS, both established by retraction below:
 * hD (LocallyOfFiniteType) is a rider on antecedent 3, proved via
   rep.uniqueUpToIso -- unconditional, not contingent on the carrier divRep
   returns.
 * hcpt IS the JacobianData.quasiCompact field, so dat-glue and dat-j name ONE
   obligation. Qualification (r4, I-1162): the half carrying that -- the mpr
   direction -- has been the producer's own implementation since 07-27
   (JacobianDataCharts.lean:216); the new content is the mp direction, which
   shows the identification cannot be undone. hcl still has no producer, so
   nothing there is discharged.

r4 REPRICING -- WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR, same session. I wrote here that the chart
parameter n is pinned to the genus by chi_moduleKSheaf UNCONDITIONALLY, so
abel-noninj owed no "we are at n = g" argument and its n > g branch was
unreachable. FALSE, refuted by a fresh-context audit (I-1176) and reproduced:
chi_moduleKSheaf CONVERTS chi = 1 - n into n = genus C, it does not SUPPLY
chi = 1 - n. With n free and no chi hypothesis the goal FAILS, and it still fails
with a representation at n in scope. My probe had hchi as a binder, so it measured
the conversion (I-1177).
   THE STANDING PRICE is ajcr-p2's: n > g is unreachable for a chart built on a
producer IN THIS TREE, because each such producer carries an hchi at its own
index. That is a claim about producers and a lane must keep them in view.
Whether an inhabitant exists at n != genus C is an OPEN inhabitation question
about DivRepAffinePullback -- mixedParamChart typechecks at arbitrary nn.
abel-noninj's live target is unchanged: the carve question, does DivScheme g
contain points where H^1 fails to vanish.

SORRY COUNT IS NOT DEBT HERE: 17 sorries, all in Challenge.lean (15, the
statement-only north star) and Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean (2). A naive count reads
AJCR as nearly done. It is not -- the gap is the three antecedents above, none of
which is a sorry.

ANSWER TO THE COSTING QUESTION, unchanged this round: none of the three closes
this week (human-facing accounting at I-0984). The items where a single round can
still produce a DECISIVE result rather than partial progress are antecedent 1's
inhabitation at one concrete V, and the abel-noninj carve question now that its
degree is pinned.

================================================================================
HISTORY FOLLOWS -- corrections in reverse chronological layers.
================================================================================

*** hcpt CLAUSE RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), refuted by ajcr-p4 (I-1007)
within minutes of my writing it. THE DEGENERACY OBSERVATION IS REAL; MY CAUSAL READING WAS
CONFOUNDED. ***

I wrote, in the self-correction below, that "hcpt is NOT an independent gate but a CONSEQUENCE of
coverage", inferred from hcpt being free at iota := PEmpty while all content sat in the
IsLocallySurjective instance. p4's refutation is decisive and I verified its pivot myself (EXIT=0):
PEmpty IS FINITE. So freeness of hcpt there is explained by the FINITE-INDEX route
(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

WHAT p4 MEASURED, more useful than my claim was: feeding the openCover route directly,
(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

CONSEQUENCE, and it strengthens the item rather than weakening it: DO NOT schedule "derive hcpt
from coverage". The two honest options are the ones the tree names -- a finite atlas, or the Abel
image (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage out of a quasi-compact DivScheme). The class-indexed atlas
needs the second, and PRICING IT is the unowned work. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j points there.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006, after a fresh-context
review of my OWN correction below). THE FOURTH ITEM IS NOT AN ANTECEDENT AT ALL -- IT IS A RIDER
ON antecedent 3, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ARGUED IT. Read this before the arithmetic
correction that follows; that correction's CONCLUSION survives but its UNIT OF PRICING was wrong. ***

WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHAT I GOT WRONG. Right: the count was 3-of-3 where the goal needs more, the
"derived, not assumed" sentence was misleading, and ajcr-p4's discharge is real. WRONG: I priced
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom as a FOURTH INDEPENDENT ANTECEDENT that p4 removed,
and justified its cheapness by the CARRIER the divRep lane happens to return today
(locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom). That argument is CONTINGENT -- it would need re-measuring
if divRep ever returned a different object.

THE UNCONDITIONAL FACT, PROBED, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound]: if divFunctor C pi n is representable by D and by D', and D'.hom is locally of finite
type, then D.hom is. Three lines -- e := rep.uniqueUpToIso rep', e.hom.left is IsIso via
Over.comp_left on hom_inv_id, then rw [<- Over.w e.hom] and infer_instance.

SO hD IS AN INVARIANT OF THE FUNCTOR AT THE PARAMETER, not a property of the chosen carrier. No
producer of rep can choose a D that fails it, and none can be blamed for one that does. The right
place for it on this board is as a RIDER ON THE rep ROW (divrep), not as an item of its own -- a
row that lists it separately INFLATES the antecedent count, which is the same error in the
opposite direction from the one I was correcting.

THE ANTECEDENT LIST OF THE GOAL, corrected again and now on unconditional grounds:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability -- CARRYING hD as a rider that costs its producer nothing.
    OPEN (divrep.u2).
 4. quasiCompact. OPEN, and see the degeneracy note below, which reprices it.

AND A DEGENERACY THAT REPRICES quasiCompact, measured on the same pass. At iota := PEmpty EVERY
explicit input of jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts is free -- hf/hdeg/V/hD/m/Z/nn by PEmpty.elim,
and hcpt free too because an empty family glues to an EMPTY space (IsEmpty => CompactSpace by
inferInstance). ALL the content sits in the single IsLocallySurjective instance. The output is
nevertheless NOT vacuous, and that was also probed (EXIT=0, same axioms): that instance at PEmpty
implies False, because JacobianData.rep yields a point of J over every test (homEquiv.symm 1)
while J.left is empty. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the assembly is sound and falsifiable, so nothing
here is a HasDivFunctor-style vacuity; (b) hcpt is NOT an independent gate of this shape but a
CONSEQUENCE of coverage -- and any future "hcpt discharged" measured at a small atlas measures
nothing at all.

ALSO CORRECTED, and it is a false absolute I repeated from p4's file: "the only declaration in
Picard/ whose conclusion is LocallyOfFiniteType is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom". There are FIVE
non-local ones plus 38 local re-derivations; the omitted ones include the very instance
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199) that Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean imports and cites to make hD free, so the
absolute is refuted by that file's own closing section. THE DEFENSIBLE FORM, which is what a board
row should say: no producer AT A CHART. Same absolute is live on row
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ("exactly ONE declaration") -- narrow it there too.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). THE ANTECEDENT COUNT ON THIS
ROW WAS THREE-OF-THREE WHERE THE GOAL NEEDS FOUR-OF-FOUR, AND ONE SENTENCE BELOW IS MISLEADING
IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. Audited ajcr-p4's finding (I-0967/I-0977); it is CORRECT. ***

THE SENTENCE TO FIX IS MINE. Below, this row says the big-site sheaf condition, the 01JJ gluing
and "BOTH finiteness certificates -- which are DERIVED from chart-level hypotheses, not assumed"
are done and kernel-checked. Read against the statements that is wrong in effect: they are derived
from chart-level hypotheses THAT NOTHING IN THE TREE PRODUCED, which is not the same as derived.
locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (JacobianDataCharts.lean:154) TAKES
hlft : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i); it was, until 67c8d24d5, the only Picard/
declaration concluding LocallyOfFiniteType at a chart, so the certificate was an assumption on
every route. PicRepDatum.lft (PicRepDatum.lean:100) is a structure FIELD -- also an assumption --
and toJacobianData (JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:87) only carries it across. So a lane that
discharged all THREE tracked antecedents would NOT have produced a JacobianData C, which is what
Challenge.lean's frozen Jacobian := (jacobianData C).J actually needs.

NOW DISCHARGED, AND IT IS A REAL DISCHARGE RATHER THAN A RELOCATION -- the part I checked hardest,
because "reduces to X" usually just moves the bill. Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean (ajcr-p4) proves
locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart: at the REAL atlas the certificate follows from
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom alone. And hD is FREE at the carrier the
divisor-representability lane returns: PROBED, imports current, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 --
LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r1 r2 b1 b2).hom closes by inferInstance ALONE at
ARBITRARY window data, via the global instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199), and DivOver (DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:113-116, :308) is an instance of
exactly that shape. So a lane producing rep supplies the fourth antecedent at the same moment at
zero cost.

WHAT REPLACES THE THREE-ITEM LIST, as the antecedent list of the GOAL:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability. OPEN (divrep.u2, ajcr-p3).
 4. hlft, chart finiteness. DISCHARGED at the real atlas, free at the rep carrier.
 5. quasiCompact. OPEN and GENUINELY A-POSTERIORI, and this is the item to watch now that 4 is
    gone. PER-CHART compactness is free at the same carrier (compactSpace_divScheme); CompactSpace
    of the GLUED object is not, and for the class-indexed (infinite) atlas the finite route
    JacobianData.ofCharts is unavailable, so it must come from the Abel image
    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage). Do not let the freeness of the per-chart form be quoted
    for the glued form -- that conflation is exactly what this correction is about.

THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: none of the three OPEN antecedents closes this week (I-0873). Item 4
was never on the list, so removing it does not shorten the critical path; what it does is make
the remaining list the true one. One caveat on the discharging file itself:
Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:65 claims "everything in it other than hf, the local-surjectivity
instance and rep is now discharged", while hcpt is an explicit hypothesis of the same definition
and the file's own :184-186 and :262-265 call it open. The :262 reading is the correct one.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context
review of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.
The route-decision conclusion SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover
`.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed. That step is
FALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on
EVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so "mk at the trivial cover" describes one PRESENTATION, not
the RANGE, and nothing follows about which classes the range contains.

AND THE ABSOLUTE FORM IS REFUTED BY A LANDED THEOREM IN THIS TREE:
PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141) proves the unit SURJECTIVE
over a field test K admitting a curve point sigma, upgraded to a MulEquiv by
PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (:186). Over such tests honesty is DISCHARGED OUTRIGHT -- vacuously
true, no etale cover needed anywhere. So "IsPlusHonest is the sheafification gap asserted of an
arbitrary section" is wrong as an absolute.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, which is narrower and better supported. The gap is at a GENERAL AFFINE BASE
WITH NO SECTION, and the tree documents exactly why:
 * the field route closes only through etale-cover cofinality in finite separable field extensions
   (Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom, EtaleCover.lean:287) -- there is NO
   general-base analogue of that cofinality;
 * EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 states plainly that for a merely quasi-finite (non-finite) etale
   cover the moving statement is FALSE, with a counterexample sketch (B = A_u x A_v over a
   2-dimensional normal local A with nontrivial local class group). So the [Module.Finite A B]
   hypothesis in the effectivity layer is load-bearing, not convenience.

SO THE OBSTRUCTION IS BASE-SHAPE, NOT ARBITRARINESS OF THE CLASS. Two consequences:
 1. the split to hand a prover lane is NOT "chart value (cheap) vs arbitrary section (blocked)" but
    "field test with a section (FREE) vs general sectionless affine base (OPEN)". The delta between
    the chart side and the coverage side is NARROWER than I priced it;
 2. antecedent 2 still owes a route decision -- which site coverage is local for -- because the
    repair still refines covers and descends, and Zariski-local surjectivity still will not absorb
    that. The conclusion stands; cite the module-finiteness counterexample, NOT the trivial-cover
    claim, when repeating it.

Also corrected, same review: I called DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean UNROOTED. It is ROOTED --
AlgebraicJacobian.lean:346 imports it at HEAD (commit 2b8cef366) and its .olean exists, so it IS
kernel-checked. Another lane rooted it while I was auditing it and I did not re-run the grep before
publishing. I-0941's step (i) is therefore already done; its step (ii) stands.

--- the original finding follows; read its trivial-cover reasoning as retracted ---

*** RANKING AMENDMENT, second reviewer pass 2026-07-29 (run 0082 session 0004, review-ajcr).
ANTECEDENT 2 IS NOT A GEOMETRY BILL, IT IS A SITE DECISION -- so the #2 slot below is
MIS-JUSTIFIED even though its position may be right. Issue I-0920. ***

The costing below is otherwise intact and should be read as it stands. This amendment changes ONE
thing: the reason antecedent 2 (dat-b B-5/B-6, local surjectivity) is expensive.

BELOW IT SAYS: "It carries the content, and its packaging is complete ... What it owes is geometry:
the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation."

MEASURED, tracing the per-point datum through its own producer chain rather than through the rows'
prose. The producer exists (exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range, rooted, sorry-free), and what
it needs reduces to ONE hypothesis: IsPlusHonest (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200). Read as a
statement, that says: for every affine open U of the test, the class restricted to U lies in the
RANGE of relPicToPicEt -- i.e. Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

That is the etale-sheafification gap, structurally:
 * picEt is built on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21), and PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a QUOTIENT
   OVER ALL ETALE COVERS -- elements are PicEtAff.mk E x;
 * PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL
   cover `.self A` alone.
So honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- precisely what the
one-step plus construction exists to permit to FAIL. The tree's only honesty mechanism agrees:
Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "does not give" says honesty holds over Spec E.Carrier and NOT over
Spec A, bought by CHANGING THE BASE, with "Nothing here performs that descent".

WHY THE CHART SIDE IS UNAFFECTED, which is what makes this a real distinction rather than a blanket
pessimism: chartValue = abelDiv * sigmaFamily * (thetaFamily^m)^{-1} (DivSchemeAbel.lean:351, read
from the definition), and honesty is discharged for each factor and closed under the group
operations. Coverage is different because chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise
(Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) quantifies over EVERY s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T);
arbitrariness is the content of coverage, and narrowing s to chart-value shape makes it circular.

CONSEQUENCE. Antecedent 2 splits into a cheap half and an out-of-reach half, and the rows conflate
them: honesty of coverage's own WITNESS is already covered; honesty of the class coverage must HIT
is the gap. The repair -- refine to the etale carrier, then descend -- changes the site from Zariski
to etale, and pic0RepresentableByOfCharts' antecedent is Zariski-local surjectivity. No leaf settles
that. It is a route question for the human/reviewer layer, and it is the third antecedent-level
obstruction found on this seam after the unrestricted-certificate fork (antecedent 1) and U2.

NOT A REFUTATION. Proving IsPlusHonest false for an arbitrary class needs a class not
Zariski-locally in relPic's image; this tree has no Brauer or nontrivial-etale-class machinery to
build one, and I did not build it. The claim is the weaker sufficient one: it is not a lemma about
the tree's own constructions, and a lane sent at it will not find a proof.

THE VERDICT BELOW ("none of the three antecedents closes this week") is unchanged and, if anything,
better supported: the antecedent that looked closest to being a bounded geometry bill is the one
that turns out to need a decision above the leaf layer.

--- the first reviewer pass's costing follows, accurate except as amended above ---

*** THE COSTING, RE-RANKED 2026-07-29 (run 0082, review-ajcr). THE THREE ANTECEDENTS ARE NOT THREE
INDEPENDENT PRICES, AND NONE OF THEM CLOSES THIS WEEK. Read this before picking a leaf. ***

WHAT IS GENUINELY SOUND, and it is worth stating first because it is unusual: pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy (Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are
sorry-free, rooted, and honest. Given the three antecedents they WOULD produce a representing scheme.
The machine is correct. Nothing feeds it.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS DO NOT COMPOSE AS THE ROWS IMPLY. Measured, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 (probes in
run 0082 session dir /probes):
 (1) `hf` = IsChartUniv (Pic0ChartPair.lean:173) is stated at a FREE `V : D.left.Opens`. At ι = PEmpty
     the whole seam call elaborates with `hf := fun i => PEmpty.elim i` -- no charts, no rep, no
     IsChartUniv. At V = bottom, injectivity is free (no nonempty test has a point of the empty open).
     So `hf` at an arbitrary V carries NO CONTENT.
     QUALIFIED by ajcr-p1 (I-0890), correctly: 'free at V = bottom' is true of the INJECTIVITY clause
     and of exists_factor, and FALSE of the fibre DATUM -- its sq field at an empty test needs
     Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C ..) over an empty base, which is true, separate, and absent from the
     tree. So the degenerate value shows a clause is cheap without exhibiting an inhabitant: CHEAP and
     SATISFIABLE come apart, and several rows on this leaf have been priced by exactly that
     conflation. The ι = PEmpty conclusion below is unaffected -- it never used V = bottom.
 (2) The seam is nonetheless NOT vacuous: at ι = PEmpty the sup sieve is BOTTOM, and the bottom sieve
     is Zariski-covering only for an EMPTY test. So ALL the content forcing the atlas to be an atlas
     sits in the LOCAL-SURJECTIVITY instance -- antecedent 2, not antecedent 1.
 (3) THE UNPRICED OBLIGATION, which no row owned before this pass: coverage
     (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise, Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) must produce
     `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ X i`, i.e. INTO `(V i : Scheme)`. So coverage must hit the SAME V at which
     `hf` was certified. chartLocus is an open of the TEST; V is an open of the DIVISOR SCHEME. Zero
     files in the tree mention both IsChartUniv and ChartsCoverLocally. Now owned by
     AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict (ajcr-p1, I-0869/I-0872).

WORSE, AND INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED WITH ajcr-p1: the only non-circular producer of `hf`,
isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre (Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:170), goes THROUGH the unrestricted
certificate -- its body is `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` with the restriction
applied afterwards. So IsChartLocusFibre implies IsOpenImmersion.presheaf of the UNRESTRICTED Abel
chart, which three headers call false (|D| is not a point). QUALIFICATION I add: that falsity is a
HEADER CLAIM, unproved -- isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective
(Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:219) takes non-injectivity as a HYPOTHESIS and is never
instantiated. So the tree holds a reduction and its conditional refutation and has connected neither.

name: blueprint-conventions
description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
---

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
- `\notready` — the Lean is **not written yet**: the node's statement stands but
  no declaration formalizes it. Mutually exclusive with `\leanok` (a node is
  never both) — remove `\notready` exactly when you add `\leanok`, i.e. the
  moment its Lean is written and checked. It is a human-facing marker of an
  intentional gap, not a DAG edge.

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

  1759	Combining the two-affine-cover cokernel bridge with the two-lattice ladder of
  1760	Chapter~\ref{chap:Algebra} along a finite morphism to the projective line yields the

  1762	computation of the cohomology of projective space --- for \(\PP^1\) itself, the

   129	\section{The relative divisor functor of the curve}
   130	\label{sec:divfam}
   131	
   132	Fix a \(k\)-algebra \(R\). A relative effective divisor on \(C_R/R\) is, locally on
   133	\(C_R\), cut out by one equation which is regular on the fibres; a local-equation system on
   134	\(C_R\) records exactly that, but on an \emph{arbitrary} pointed cover, and with regularity
   135	asked in the stalks of \(C_R\) rather than on the fibres.  For the auxiliary pinned-window
   136	presentation, a refinement by finitely many basic opens of the two pinned charts is paired
   137	with a certificate asserting that the resulting colength modules are finite projective over
   138	\(R\) of constant rank \(n\).  The widened \(\Div^{\,n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\) carrier instead
   139	records an arbitrary affine-open cover of the relative curve and its local certificates.
   140	In either presentation the certificate is the proposed formal
   141	analogue of \(R\)-flatness with fibres of degree \(n\) in Kleiman's Definition of
   142	\(\Div^{\,n}_{X/S}\).
   143	
   144	\begin{definition}[Auxiliary finite chart cover data]
   145	  \label{def:finCoverData}
   146	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData, AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.pieces,
   147	    AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.cover₀, AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.cover₁,
   148	    AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData.isAffineOpen_pieces,
   149	    AlgebraicGeometry.le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one}
   150	  \uses{def:relCurve, def:relCover, def:fiberTwoCover}
   151	  \leanok
   152	  This auxiliary pinned-window datum on \(C_R\) consists of finitely many sections
   153	  \(h^0_1,\dots,h^0_{m_0} \in \struct{}(V_0^R)\) and \(h^1_1,\dots,h^1_{m_1} \in
   154	  \struct{}(V_1^R)\), together with coefficients \(a^\iota_j\) in the same rings satisfying
   155	  the two partition identities
   156	  \[
   157	    \sum_{j} a^0_j h^0_j = 1 \ \text{ in } \struct{}(V_0^R), \qquad
   158	    \sum_{j} a^1_j h^1_j = 1 \ \text{ in } \struct{}(V_1^R).
   159	  \]
   160	  Its \emph{pieces} are the basic opens \(P_j := D(h^\iota_j) \subseteq V_\iota^R\), indexed

    11	# The widened `DivFamZar` (R2, human decision I-0492)
    12	
    13	The endpoint of the widening.  `IsLocallyCertifiedAff` is the locally-certified predicate
    14	whose local certificates are carried by **arbitrary affine-open covers** rather than by basic
    15	opens of a fixed pair of pinned `P¹` charts, and `DivFamZarAff` is its `DivEq` quotient —
    16	the object the human decision of 2026-07-28 is about.
    17	
    18	## Why this is strictly weaker than the old predicate, which is the whole point
    19	
    20	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) turns every old cover datum into
    21	a widened one, and `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean` migrates the CERTIFICATE on top of it, so
    22	`isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified` holds: anything the old
    23	predicate certified, the new one certifies.  The converse fails, and its failure is exactly
    24	the content of R2 — a divisor straddling both pinned vertical fibres has no chart-typed
    25	certificate (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 4 §4.3, on-stratum witness at every `g ≥ 2`)
    26	but does admit an affine-open one, because `supp D` is finite over `R` and therefore lies in a
    27	single affine open of `C ×_k Spec R` (Stacks `0B8B`).
    28	
    29	So `DivFamZarAff` is the value on which the divisor functor can be a Zariski sheaf over an
    30	ARBITRARY field, with no `|P¹(k)| ≥ n + 2` hypothesis anywhere — the field-uniform fix.
    31	
    32	## The two relocated obligations (I-0492 clause 4)
    33	
    34	* **(i) fibrewise-finite support.** NOT a field of anything here.  It is not implied by
    35	  what a `LocalEquations` carries (`d.eqn ≡ r` for a non-unit `r ∈ R` is germ-regular with a
    36	  whole fibre curve in its support), so it must come from the seed's own degree data.  It
    37	  enters as an explicit hypothesis at the point of use, never as carrier data: concretely as
    38	  the `hfib` argument of `AffAdaptation.isCertified_of_swallowedBy`
    39	  (`DivisorFamilyAffAssemble.lean`) and as `AffCoverData.SwallowedBy`
    40	  (`DivisorFamilyAffSwallow.lean`).  Neither is a field of anything in this file.
    41	* **(ii) what the fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying.** Discharged in
    42	  `DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean` (`exists_mem_pieces` from the joint cover,
    43	  `flat_sections_pieces` from the flat structure morphism) and in
    44	  `DivisorFamilyAffPerPiece.lean` (the whole per-piece layer, from openness and affineness).
    45	
    46	## Main declarations
    47	
    48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff` — a certified family over a widened cover.
    49	* `AlgebraicGeometry.IsLocallyCertifiedAff` — the widened locally-certified predicate.
    50	* `IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq` — it respects divisor equality.
    51	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff` — the widened functor value, with `mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`
    52	  and `picClass`.
    53	
    54	The comparison with the chart-typed predicate — `isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_isLocallyCertified`
    55	and `DivFamZar.toAff` — is in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`, which imports this file.
    56	* `AlgebraicGeometry.isLocallyCertifiedAff_of_forall_prime_exists_away` — the pointwise gate,
    57	  one base point at a time, over the widened predicate.
    58	-/

    76	/-! ## Certified families over a widened cover -/
    77	
    78	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over a widened cover**: a local-equation
    79	system, an affine-open cover datum, an adaptation, and the certificate.  The cover is part of
    80	the data (it is chosen per family), exactly as the old `adaptation` field bundled its own
    81	`FinCoverData`. -/

    83	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/

    85	  /-- The affine-open cover carrying the certificate. -/

    94	variable {C R}
    95	
    96	/-- **The widened locally-certified pin.**  Identical in shape to `IsLocallyCertified`
    97	(`DivisorFamilyZar.lean`) — a span-`⊤` family `g : Fin m → R` with certified families over
    98	the away localizations, divisor-equal to the pulled system — except that the local
    99	certificates live over ARBITRARY AFFINE-OPEN covers.
   100	
   101	The base-side structure is untouched on purpose: R2 widens where the pieces live on the
   102	CURVE, and changes nothing about the Zariski cover of the base. -/
   103	def IsLocallyCertifiedAff (n : ℕ) (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) : Prop :=
   104	  ∃ (m : ℕ) (g : Fin m → R), Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤ ∧
   105	    ∀ i : Fin m,
   106	      haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   107	        isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   108	      ∃ G : CertifiedDivisorFamilyAff C (Localization.Away (g i)) n,
   109	        Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq G.eqns
   110	          (d.pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
   111	            (Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_isOpenImmersion
   112	              (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) d))
   113	
   114	/-- **The widened pin respects divisor equality** — the local `DivEq`s transport through
   115	`divEq_pullback`, verbatim as in the chart-typed case. -/
   116	theorem IsLocallyCertifiedAff.of_divEq {n : ℕ} {d d' : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   117	    (hd : IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d) (h : Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq d d') :
   118	    IsLocallyCertifiedAff n d' := by
   119	  obtain ⟨m, g, hg, hG⟩ := hd
   120	  refine ⟨m, g, hg, fun i => ?_⟩
   121	  haveI : IsOpenImmersion (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i))) :=
   122	    isOpenImmersion_relCurveMap_away C R (Localization.Away (g i)) (g i)
   123	  obtain ⟨G, hGdiv⟩ := hG i
   124	  exact ⟨G, hGdiv.trans
   125	    (Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_pullback (relCurveMap C R (Localization.Away (g i)))
   126	      h _ _)⟩

   128	/-! ## The comparison with the chart-typed predicate
   129	
   130	`FinCoverData.toAffCoverData` (`DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean`) already migrates the COVER
   131	sorry-free, and the adaptation's equations and `eqn_rel` transport with it because the pieces
   132	are literally the same opens, only reindexed along `finSumFinEquiv`.

   134	The migration of the CERTIFICATE is landed too, in `DivisorFamilyAffCompare.lean`
   135	(`DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_toAff`, all seven clauses).  Clauses (c1) are `rfl` at the
   136	relabelled index; the glued clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transport along `LinearEquiv.piCongrLeft`
   137	in its `symm` direction, which evaluates cast-free, so the intertwining with
   138	`deltaLeft`/`deltaRight` is componentwise and `Module.rankAtStalk` invariance is
   139	`rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv`.  No clause changes, only the index does.
   140	
   141	A predecessor docstring here estimated that transport at about a hundred lines of equalizer
   142	bookkeeping.  That was wrong by an order of magnitude and the reason generalises: arrange the
   143	reindexed cover so its pieces are DEFINITIONALLY the original pieces at the relabelled index,
   144	and the overlap data at `(i, j)` becomes `rfl`-equal to the original at `(e i, e j)`, because
   145	reindexing acts diagonally on the pair index.  Then no intertwining lemma exists to prove. -/

200	  have step1 := Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_pullbackEqn_congr hcomp₂ d ζ

   224	def divFamZarSetoid : Setoid {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations //
   225	    IsLocallyCertified C R π n d} where

   232	(`informal/spec-dd-2.md`, Addendum 2): locally certified local-equation systems of

    10	# Certified base change on the widened cover (R2, human decision I-0492)
    11	
    12	The seven certificate clauses of `AffAdaptation.IsCertified` transport along an arbitrary test
    13	change `R → R'`.  This is the last structural piece the widened value needed: without it
    14	`DivFamZarAff` is a type with no functoriality, and nothing downstream can base-change a
    15	widened class.
    16	
    17	## Two definitional identities do most of the work
    18	
    19	Both were probed and hold on the nose, which is why this file is short:
    20	
    21	* the base-changed overlap **is** the preimage of the overlap
    22	  (`(D.baseChange R').pieces i ⊓ (D.baseChange R').pieces j = relCurveMap ⁻¹ᵁ (pieces i ⊓
    23	  pieces j)` by `rfl`, since `⁻¹ᵁ` commutes with `⊓` definitionally on `Opens`);
    24	* the pulled colength **is** the quotient `relQuotBaseChangeAff` lands in.
    25	
    26	So the widened colength and overlap transports are the SAME declaration
    27	(`AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange`) at two different opens, where the chart-typed layer
    28	needed `pieceQuotBaseChange` and a separately-constructed `ovlQuotBaseChange` conjugated
    29	through the overlap generator.
    30	
    31	## What is reused verbatim
    32	
    33	Clauses (c2)/(c3)/(c4) ride the abstract `FlatCokernel` keystones
    34	(`LinearMap.ker_lTensor_eq_of_flat_coker`, `LinearMap.tensorKerEquivOfFlatCoker`,
    35	`LinearMap.quotRangeBaseChangeEquiv`) and the two square-transport lemmas
    36	(`LinearEquiv.map_ker_of_comp_eq`, `LinearEquiv.range_eq_map_range_of_comp_eq`).  All are
    37	stated for bare modules and know nothing about covers, so the widening does not touch them.
    38	
    39	## Main declarations
    40	
    41	* `AffAdaptation.colengthBaseChange`, `ovlColengthBaseChange` — the (c1) and overlap
    42	  transports, both `AffCoverData.pieceQuotBaseChange`.
    43	* `AffAdaptation.chartProdBaseChange`, `ovlProdBaseChange` — the product transports.
    44	* `AffAdaptation.delta_baseChange_comm` — `δ`-naturality, a `funext` over the pair index.
    45	* `AffAdaptation.gluedBaseChange` and the (c2)/(c3)/(c4) transports.
    46	* `AffAdaptation.isCertified_pullback` — **the certificate base-changes**, all seven clauses.
    47	-/

    73	/-- **Base change of a piece colength**: `R' ⊗[R] colength j ≃ₐ[R'] (pullback).colength j`.

    68	    x_0^{m_0+l_0} \cdots x_r^{m_r+l_r},
    69	\]

\section{The Jacobian as an abelian variety}

\begin{definition}[Jacobian]
  \label{def:jacobian}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian}
  The \emph{Jacobian} \(\Jac(C)\) of a smooth proper curve \(C\) over \(k\) is the identity
  component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) of the relative Picard scheme of \(C\) over \(k\): the \(k\)-scheme
  representing (the fppf-sheafification of) the functor of degree-zero line bundles on \(C\).
\end{definition}

Fix a \(k\)-algebra \(R\). A relative effective divisor on \(C_R/R\) is, locally on
\(C_R\), cut out by one equation which is regular on the fibres; a local-equation system on
\(C_R\) records exactly that, but on an \emph{arbitrary} pointed cover, and with regularity
asked in the stalks of \(C_R\) rather than on the fibres.  For the auxiliary pinned-window
presentation, a refinement by finitely many basic opens of the two pinned charts is paired
with a certificate asserting that the resulting colength modules are finite projective over
\(R\) of constant rank \(n\).  The widened \(\Div^{\,n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\) carrier instead
records an arbitrary affine-open cover of the relative curve and its local certificates.
In either presentation the certificate is the proposed formal
analogue of \(R\)-flatness with fibres of degree \(n\) in Kleiman's Definition of
\(\Div^{\,n}_{X/S}\).

\begin{definition}[The locally certified divisor functor \(\Div^{\,n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\)]
  \label{def:divFamZar}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar, AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.mk,
    AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.mk_eq_mk_iff, AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZar.picClass,
    AlgebraicGeometry.DivFam.toZar}
  \uses{def:isLocallyCertified, lem:localEquations_divEq, def:certifiedDivisorFamily}
  \leanok
  The value at \(R\) of the \emph{locally certified} divisor functor is
  \[
    \Div^{\,n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(R) \;:=\;
      \bigl\{\, d \text{ locally certified of degree } n \text{ on } C_R \,\bigr\} \big/ \sim ,
  \]
  the quotient by divisor equality (well posed by \ref{def:isLocallyCertified}). The Picard
  class descends to it, and passing from a global to a local certificate gives a natural
  comparison \(\Div^{\,n}(R) \to \Div^{\,n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}(R)\) compatible with the Picard
  class.

  This is the carrier every statement below uses. The reason is
  Theorem~\ref{thm:isCertified_chart_obstruction}: the condition ``carries a global
  certificate'' is not local on \(\Spec R\), so \(\Div^{\,n}\) cannot be a Zariski sheaf on
  affine test algebras, whereas \(\Div^{\,n}_{\mathrm{Zar}}\) is local on the base by
  construction.
\end{definition}
\begin{proof}

Combining the two-affine-cover cokernel bridge with the two-lattice ladder of
